what_happened: A docs job to fix newcomer gaps on the firstmate study site page was rejected at final verification. One of 8 acceptance criteria was unmet: criterion 7, which said the producer's report must list the commands it ran, including `cargo run -p xtask -- site`. The verifier raised one major finding: it could not confirm the producer reported those commands. No failed checks are listed. The other seven criteria were not reported as unmet, so the page work itself was probably fine.
cause: Criteria are written without asking whether the verifier can observe the evidence. The producer's report is a producer-side artifact that the verifier does not receive, so the criterion cannot be satisfied or checked however well the work is done. Nothing at the reading or planning stage checks each criterion against what the verifier can see, namely the diff, the repo state and its own command runs. Process claims such as "commands ran" are also a weak form of criterion, because the verifier can run the command itself.
prevention: Add a check at reading acceptance that flags any criterion whose evidence is the producer's report, its transcript or its self-described actions. The reading must either rewrite it as an outcome the verifier can observe (for example, the generated site output exists and `cargo run -p xtask -- site` exits cleanly when the verifier runs it) or pass the producer's report to the verifier explicitly as an input. The check should also require each criterion to name its evidence source from a fixed list of what the verifier can see.
proposed_request: Re-run the firstmate study site page newcomer-gaps fix (job 20261027-122909-37mg), with criterion 7 changed. Drop "the producer's report lists the commands it ran". Replace it with: running `cargo run -p xtask -- site` on the final snapshot succeeds and regenerates the firstmate study page, and the repo's tests, clippy and fmt pass. Keep the other seven criteria as they were. Do not make any criterion depend on the producer's report.
